title: K2 Tank Parts: Which Korean Companies Make the Engine, Gun and Fire Control (Poland Exports)
content:
Poland ordered 1,000 K2 tanks under a framework contract in 2022. Of that, 180 have been delivered under the first implementation contract and a second 180 worth about $6.5 billion is under way. Here is which companies make the main parts, and what could not be confirmed. The engine, gun, fire control system and armor-piercing round each have an identifiable maker; the transmission, autoloader and suspension need caveats.

1. Engine — HD Construction Equipment

The DV27K engine was made by HD Hyundai Infracore. Shareholders approved its merger with HD Hyundai Construction Equipment in September 2025, and it now trades as HD Construction Equipment (KRX: 267270), which is why searching the old name returns "delisted." The engine in Polish export tanks is also Korean-made.

2. Transmission — still German for exports

Korea began developing a domestic powerpack in 2005 with a budget of 96.4 billion won (48.8 billion for the engine and 47.6 billion for the transmission). The engine was localized, but the transmission failed a 320-hour durability test, with a defect at 306 hours that ended the test. The first three production batches therefore use German RENK transmissions, and RENK has announced more than €70 million in additional orders for HSWL 295 transmissions for Polish K2s. A domestic transmission is scheduled from the fourth production batch for the Korean army. The domestic test result and the Polish contract specification are separate facts and are not linked here.

3. Gun — Hyundai Wia

The 120mm smoothbore gun is made by Hyundai Wia, whose defense business page lists tank guns for the K2 and K1A1.

4. Autoloader — maker not identified

Neither Hyundai Wia's nor Hyundai Rotem's official product pages name the maker of the autoloader. That means we could not identify it in the materials we checked, not that it is secret, and we did not guess a company.

5. Fire control system — Hanwha Systems

The equipment that keeps aim while the tank is moving is made by Hanwha Systems, which has built sights and ballistic computers since the K1 era. It has a 203.1 billion won supply contract for the fire control system of Polish K2s, signed together with Hyundai Rotem.

6. K279 armor-piercing round — Poongsan

The K279 is a tungsten penetrator round that sheds its casing in flight. Poongsan makes it, and the penetrator technology was co-developed by the Agency for Defense Development and Poongsan in 1993. That Poongsan makes the K279 is not the same as the K279 being supplied under the Polish contract. Reports say ammunition is part of the second contract, but we found no official source naming the K279 and Poongsan.

7. Suspension and system integration

The K2 is the first tank to adopt a semi-active hydropneumatic suspension throughout, letting the hull crouch and rise. No K2 supplier could be confirmed. Hyundai Mobis makes similar suspensions for other vehicles such as the K21, but a direct K2 delivery is not confirmed, so no company is named. Hyundai Rotem assembles the finished tank and signed the second Polish implementation contract in August 2025.

Poland K2 contracts: what is confirmed

StageDetail
Framework contract2022, 1,000 tanks in scale; confirmed implementation contracts are 180 + 180 = 360 tanks
First contract180 tanks delivered
Second contract180 tanks, about $6.5 billion, 2026–2030; 116 K2GF and 64 K2PL, with about 110 built in Changwon and about 60 assembled in Poland; the value includes support vehicles, logistics and training
Third contract210 tanks in progress (120 from Korea and 90 from Poland, planned 2026–2034), reported
IraqAbout 250 tanks under consideration, reported, not a confirmed contract

Won conversions of the second contract vary by report (for example 8.7464 trillion or 8.9485 trillion won) and move with the exchange rate, so dollars are used here.

What this post could and could not confirm

Confirmed: the makers of the engine, gun and fire control system, and the size of the first and second Polish implementation contracts. Not confirmed: who makes the autoloader and suspension, whether the K279 is part of the Polish contract, and the status of the third contract and Iraq. The information was checked against public sources on September 20–21, 2026, so later changes may not be reflected.

Quick FAQ

Did Poland buy 1,000 K2 tanks?
1,000 is the scale of the 2022 framework contract. The confirmed implementation contracts are 180 delivered tanks and a second batch of 180, 360 in total.

Is the K2 transmission Korean-made?
Not yet for exports. The Polish K2PL uses a Korean engine with a German RENK transmission. A domestic transmission (SNT Dynamics) is scheduled for the Korean army from the fourth production batch.

Was HD Hyundai Infracore delisted?
It merged with HD Hyundai Construction Equipment in January 2026 and now trades as HD Construction Equipment (KRX: 267270). The engine business carried over.

Who makes the K2's autoloader?
It could not be identified in the official materials checked, so no company is named.

Companies named are disclosed or reported suppliers; parts with no confirmed supplier are labeled as such. Images are reconstructions based on public information, not an actual teardown. Sources include Hyundai Rotem (Aug 1, 2025), Asia Economy (Feb 2026), RENK, Hanwha Systems, Hyundai Wia's defense business page, and The Guru and Financial News (Jul 2026).
